source_snapshot.message:
feat(mcp): make ix mcp a superset of the per-host plugin tools

Prerequisite for retiring the six plugins' own tool implementations. The
plugins never shared one tool surface, so delegating to `ix mcp` as it
stood would have removed tools from three of them:

  codex, cursor    23 tools, identical — lossless today
  gemini           23, of which decide/ingest/query/status were not served
  openclaw         17, of which decide/docs_tool/ingest/neighbors/query
  opencode         17, same as openclaw
  claude            0 — skills only, nothing to migrate

`ix_decide` and `ix_ingest` were the only real capability gaps and are now
served. Three exclusions are deliberate: `ix_query` is the deprecated
command the CLI docs tell agents not to use; `ix_neighbors` and
`ix_docs_tool` are composites of callers/callees/depends and of overview,
all served individually. `ix_status` is gemini's name for `ix_health`.

Pro tools are now advertised only when @ix/pro actually resolves.
`ix_briefing` and `ix_decisions` were offered to every install while
answering "requires Ix Pro" on every call, which an agent cannot tell
apart from a real failure; `ix_decide` would have been a third. OSS
installs see 22 tools, Pro installs 25 — both observed on one machine,
since the global @ix/pro resolves for the CLI but not under vitest.

`ix mcp doctor` reports the count this install actually advertises rather
than the theoretical maximum.

docs/mcp-plugin-consolidation.md records what MCP can absorb (~15.3k lines
of tool implementations) and what it cannot (~10.6k lines of agents, hooks,
skills and commands, which have no MCP equivalent and stay host-specific),
plus the order the migration has to happen in.
